items.h: Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) ruled out for Sunday
items.s: Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns. Harrison wasn't able to practice throughout the week due to a hamstring injury, so it's unsurprising that he has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Browns. He hasn't been getting many targets for Houston recently, but his absence may still open up some opportunities for Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte this week.

items.h: Ruled out for Sunday's game
items.s: Harrison (hamstring) is ruled out for Sunday's game against the Browns. Harrison's absence leaves more snaps for some combination of Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte and Tank Dell, all of whom were productive last week in a win over the Chargers. C.J. Stroud has been spreading the ball around and putting up big numbers in the process, with even Nico Collins seeing his target share suffer as a result. Harrison is unlikely to handle a full-time role even when he gets back to full strength.

items.h: Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) not practicing Friday
items.s: Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) is not practicing for the Houston Texans Friday according to Aaron Wilson. Harrison Jr. has yet to progress enough to participate in any practice for head coach DeMeco Ryans, putting the wideout's availability in question for Sunday's contest against the Browns.

items.h: Not seen at Friday's practice
items.s: Harrison (hamstring) wasn't spotted during the portion of Friday's practice open to the media, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports. Harrison also missed Thursday's session, so the WR's apparent absence Friday doesn't bode well for his chances of playing Sunday against the Browns. If Harrison ends up out this weekend, Xavier Hutchinson, Tank Dell and Kayshon Boutte would be available to handle WR targets that don't go to top option Nico Collins.

items.h: Marvin Harrison Jr. Ruled Out for Week 10
items.s: Houston Texans wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) has been ruled out for his team's Week 10 matchup against the Cleveland Browns due to a hamstring injury, per Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston. Harrison Jr. has played a limited role in the Houston offense since being acquired from the Arizona Cardinals in early October, recording six catches for 60 yards and a touchdown on 11 targets across three games. This latest injury is another setback for the 24-year-old, who will miss a valuable opportunity to establish himself in the Texans' passing game in Week 10. With Harrison Jr. sidelined, Houston wideouts Nico Collins, Tank Dell, Xavier Hutchinson, and Kayshon Boutte could all see…

items.h: Downgrades to 'DNP' Thursday
items.s: Harrison (hamstring) didn't practice Thursday, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports. Harrison was limited Wednesday, so the WR's downgrade in participation a day later clouds his status for Sunday's game against the Browns. In three outings since arriving in a trade with the Cardinals, the No. 4 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft has combined to catch six of his 11 targets for 60 yards and a TD in in that span.

items.h: Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) downgraded to non-participant Thursday
items.s: Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) was downgraded to a non-participant at practice on Thursday. It looks like Harrison is trending the wrong way for Week 10, as he was downgraded to a non-participant at practice on Thursday after being limited by a hamstring issue on Wednesday. His absence this week would clear the way for Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte to see more opportunities on Houston's offense.

items.h: Marvin Harrison Jr. Sits Out of Practice on Thursday
items.s: Houston Texans wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday, according to Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Sports. Harrison was limited in practice on Wednesday, so his status on Thursday is a downgrade and puts his status in doubt for the Week 10 game on Sunday against the hosting Cleveland Browns. Meanwhile, fellow receiver Tank Dell was upgraded to a full participant and will not have any restrictions this weekend in his third game back from a gruesome knee injury in 2024 that caused him to miss the entire 2025 campaign. If the 24-year-old Harrison cannot play against Cleveland, Dell, Kayshon Boutte, and Xavier Hutchinson would see more snaps behind WR1 Nico Collins…

items.h: Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) limited in practice Wednesday
items.s: Marvin Harrison Jr. was limited in practice on Wednesday. Harrison is on track to be good to go in Week 10. He remains off the fantasy radar in his current role.

items.h: Dealing with hamstring injury
items.s: Harrison (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports. It's a new injury for the Texans' newest wideout, who has produced just six catches for 60 yards and a touchdown on 11 targets through three games with Houston. Harrison ran just 14 routes on 40 dropbacks last Sunday against the Chargers, tying him with Kayshon Boutte for fourth among Texans wideouts. Xavier Hutchinson and Tank Dell appear to have emerged as the Nos. 2 and 3 receivers behind Nico Collins.

items.h: Marvin Harrison Jr. Limited in Texans Practice on Wednesday
items.s: Houston Texans wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) is dealing with a hamstring injury and was listed as a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, according to Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Sports. Harrison is dealing with a new injury as the team prepares to face the Cleveland Browns in Week 10 on Sunday. The injury does not appear to be serious enough to keep the 24-year-old former first-rounder from playing, but fantasy managers who still have the Ohio State product rostered should be leaving him on the bench yet again. He played nearly half of the Texans' offensive snaps in the Week 9 win over the Los Angeles Chargers, but he secured only two of his three targets for 20 yards a…

items.h: Marvin Harrison Jr. Droppable in Most Fantasy Leagues
items.s: Houston wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. is not worth holding in all standard fantasy leagues, and lackluster results of late also make him droppable in some deeper leagues. Across his first three games with the Texans, Harrison has just six catches for 60 yards and a touchdown over 11 targets. He played 32 offensive snaps in Week 9, which was the most he's logged with Houston, but also still just 45.7% of the team's total - it also came in a blowout win, and he was behind several other pass catchers. Harrison is only worth stashing in really deep leagues at this point, and he's not even a confident starting option in those leagues. Look elsewhere for fantasy wideout help in the meantime.

items.h: Marvin Harrison Jr. quiet in win Sunday
items.s: Marvin Harrison Jr. caught 2-of-3 targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 44-22 win over the Los Angeles Chargers. Houston's offense was on a roll on Sunday, but Harrison wasn't able to take part in that. He finished with just 20 yards in the teams' win over the Chargers, and it looks like there are several other wideouts on the team ahead of him in the pecking order at this point. He shouldn't be rostered in most league formats at this point.

items.h: Two catches during blowout win
items.s: Harrison caught two of three targets for 20 yards during Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers. Harrison ranked seventh on the team in targets, and although C.J. Stroud connected with four different wide receivers for five total touchdowns, Harrison was not one of them. Harrison has now reeled in six of 11 targets for 60 yards and a score over three contests with the Texans, and he will remain hard to trust from a fantasy perspective in Week 10 versus Cleveland.

items.h: Marvin Harrison Jr. Only an Option in Deep Leagues
items.s: Houston Texans wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. cost the team some significant draft capital to bring in via trade earlier this season, but the move hasn't fully paid off yet. In his two games with the team, he has eight targets, but just four catches for 40 yards. He did get into the end zone on his one catch for six yards in Week 7 against the Giants, but he was still limited to only 13 snaps in Week 7 after playing just 12 offensive snaps in Week 6. Hopefully, the bye week gave him time to get more involved, and his role could increase now that he's been around the team for several weeks. However, Harrison is still only WR62 in our RotoBaller Week 9 projections. In a mostly neutral…

items.h: Marvin Harrison Jr. Eyes More Production After Team's Bye Week
items.s: Houston wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. will look to start producing a bit more for his new team after the team had its bye in Week 8. Since being traded to the Texans, Harrison has eight targets, but just four catches for 40 yards. His lone catch in Week 7 against the Giants was a touchdown, so that's maybe another reason why his fantasy value is rising a bit. Harrison logged just 12 offensive snaps in Week 6, then played 13 snaps in Week 7. It's fair to assume his playing time and role could improve now that he's been around the team for several weeks. Harrison is still only WR66 in our RotoBaller Week 9 projections. He has a pretty average fantasy matchup coming against the Chargers,…

items.h: Judging overreactions to NFL Week 7: McCarthy-led Giants are NFC East favorites?
items.s: Will J.J. McCarthy bring the Giants to the postseason? Are the Vikings headed for a bye? How bad do the 49ers need Mike Evans back? Let's overreact to Sunday's games.

items.h: Marvin Harrison Jr. catches touchdown Sunday
items.s: Marvin Harrison Jr. caught 1-of-4 targets for six yards and a touchdown in the Texans 27-21 loss against the Giants. For fantasy managers desperate enough to start Harrison, fortunately his lone catch was in the end zone. He remains in the WR4/WR5 range.

items.h: Gets first TD with Texans
items.s: Harrison caught one of four targets for a six-yard touchdown in Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants. In his second game since being acquired from Arizona via trade, Harrison scored his first touchdown with the Texans. His six-yard touchdown catch in the second quarter was Harrison's lone catch in a game during which six different wide receivers recorded at least one reception for the Texans. Harrison will have an opportunity to increase his knowledge of the playbook during a Week 8 bye and potentially earn more playing time in Houston's crowded wide-receiver room.

items.h: Marvin Harrison Jr. Hard to Start in Week 7
items.s: Houston Texans wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. is coming off his first full week of practice with his new team after being traded from Arizona to Houston just over a week ago. In his Texans debut, he caught three of four targets for 34 yards in Week 6's 34-31 win over the Jaguars. He played 12 snaps (19%) in that game, but he should be more familiar with the playbook and have a larger role this week against the Giants. Since he's still ramping up, though, and the Texans have many options at receiver, it's hard to trust him in fantasy lineups at this point. Harrison is the No. 54 WR this week in RotoBaller's PPR rankings, making him only a deep-league play at this point. He has enough…

items.h: Marvin Harrison Jr. Was Frustrated With his Performance in Arizona
items.s: Arizona Cardinals general manager Monti Ossenfort did not give a clear answer when asked if former wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. asked for a trade, saying that the team had "a lot of positive discussions with Marv" before they traded him to the Houston Texans, according to Tyler Drake of Arizona Sports. "I think Marv really was always just trying to do more. And Marv always wanted to perform. Marv's heart and what he wants, and for our team and for his career, we're always, 'Hey, he wanted to perform.' I think there was some frustration on his end that he wasn't performing and wasn't producing like he felt. And so, I think those were conversations that happened throughout the weeks,…

items.h: Marvin Harrison Jr. Worth Holding Following Trade to Houston?
items.s: In his first game as a member of the Houston Texans in Week 6, wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. recorded three catches for 34 yards on four targets. Harrison Jr. got off to a nightmarish start to the season with the Arizona Cardinals, hauling in just five catches for 85 yards and a touchdown on 13 targets across four games. The 24-year-old has also largely been a disappointment for fantasy managers since being selected by Arizona fourth overall in the 2024 NFL Draft. However, Harrison Jr. may have new life now that he's been traded. With star wideout Nico Collins operating as the primary X receiver in Houston, Harrison Jr. could be freed up to play a more versatile role in the Texans'…

items.h: Marvin Harrison Jr. hauls in three passes in Week 6
items.s: Marvin Harrison Jr. caught 3-of-4 targets for 34 yards in a 34-31 win over Jacksonville. Harrison was making his debut for Houston and was figured to only factor into a handful of plays. Despite that, his three receptions tie a season high and the Texans are clearly high on the 24-year-old. Harrison and the Texans will take on the Giants in Week 7.

items.h: Three catches in Houston debut
items.s: Harrison caught three of four targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 34-31 win over the Jaguars. Making his Texans debut, Harrison wasn't especially productive on his own, but quarterback C.J. Stroud seemed to benefit from his presence and spread the ball around to 10 different pass catchers. The three grabs still tied Harrison's season high, giving him something to build on as he looks to put his disappointing Cardinals tenure behind him. The two former Ohio State teammates will look to re-buiild their chemistry further in Week 7 against the Giants.

items.h: Confirmed for team debut Sunday
items.s: Harrison is active for Sunday's game against the Jaguars in London. Just as head coach DeMeco Ryans indicated would be the case earlier in the week, Harrison will be cleared to make his Texans debut right away after being acquired from the Cardinals on Monday. Since he hasn't had much time to get up to speed with his new playbook, Harrison is expected to be eased into the mix Sunday with a light snap count, per Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network. Eventually, the No. 4 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft could settle in as the Texans' No. 2 wideout behind Nico Collins.

items.h: Marvin Harrison Jr. Only a Deep-League Option in Texans Debut
items.s: Houston Texans wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. is set to make his debut for his new team with a limited package against the Jaguars in Week 6. Coach DeMeco Ryans praised the receiver's work to learn the team's playbook after he was acquired earlier this week, but he also said, "Don't expect him to come out and play all 60 snaps in the game, but we'll make sure he gets what he needs." While the team will want to showcase its new addition, Harrison will be a high-risk option since he is still just ramping up with his new team's playbook and terminology. He only had five catches for 85 yards and one touchdown in four games with the Cardinals before the trade, so he may need time to settle…

items.h: Marvin Harrison Jr. Set for Limited Role in Texans Debut
items.s: Houston Texans wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. will make his team debut Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Wembley Stadium, although his playing time will be managed as he adjusts to his new offense. According to Aaron Wilson, head coach DeMeco Ryans said Harrison will have a specific package of plays and cautioned against expecting him to play all 60 snaps. The former first-round pick has had little time to practice with Houston since arriving from Arizona, where he caught just five passes for 85 yards and one touchdown on 13 targets through four games this season. Harrison reunites with former Ohio State quarterback C.J. Stroud and joins a receiving group led by Nico Collins.…

items.h: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed Wednesday that Harrison will make his team debut Sunday versus the Jaguars in London, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports.
items.s: Harrison was inactive for the Cardinals' Week 5 loss to the Lions before he was officially traded Monday to the Texans along with a 2027 sixth-round pick in exchange for 2027 second- and seventh-round picks. After passing his physical, Harrison took the field Wednesday for his first practice with the Texans. Houston may limit Harrison's snaps to some degree in Week 6, but once he fully absorbs his new playbook, he could make a push for the No. 2 spot on the depth chart at receiver behind Nico Collins.

items.h: The Texans acquired Harrison and a 2027 sixth-round pick from the Cardinals on Sunday in exchange for 2027 second- and seventh-round selections, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
items.s: After Adam Schefter of ESPN reported Saturday that Arizona had agreed to deal Harrison to an undisclosed team, Houston had been bandied about in the rumor mill as the organization in question. Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed following Sunday's win over the Titans that Harrison is indeed on his way to Houston, with Rapoport providing the particulars of the deal shortly thereafter. In Houston, Harrison may need some time to acclimate himself to a new offensive scheme, though he does have plenty of familiarity with quarterback C.J. Stroud from their time in college together at Ohio…

items.h: A trade for Harrison will not be completed "until after Sunday's games are played," but the Cardinals "feel comfortable enough" knowing it will occur that they will deactivate him for Sunday's game against the Lions,…
items.s: Harrison's long-term outlook is firmly up in the air after it was announced earlier Saturday that he will be traded to an unspecified team, but per the latest report, "The one certainty is that Harrison's time in Arizona is done." Michael Wilson and Trey McBride figure to remain plenty busy in the passing game, and Harrison's absence will open up some opportunities for Kendrick Bourne and presumably Jalen Brooks.

items.h: The Cardinals are "finalizing a deal to trade Harrison" to an unspecified team, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
items.s: Harrison's destination is unclear, but he is on the move after spending two seasons and the early portion of the current campaign in Arizona. Per the report, the Cardinals informed Harrison "that he will be inactive for Sunday's game against the Lions as details of the trade are finalized," so one way or another he will not see action in Week 5.

items.h: What to know before setting your lineup for Week 5: Is Maye back? Start Wilson?
items.s: Adam Rank catches you up on the vital information and insight needed to make tough lineup decisions in Week 5.

items.h: Harrison caught one of four targets for 12 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 36-24 loss to the Giants.
items.s: The struggling third-year WR hit paydirt for the first time this season, connecting with Jacoby Brissett for his only catch of the afternoon in the first quarter to cap the Cardinals' opening drive. Harrison has only five receptions through four games for just 85 yards on a meager 13 targets, and a change of scenery increasingly seems like it might offer his best chance to salvage his career. He'll try to earn a bigger role in the passing game in Week 5 at home against the Lions.

items.h: Harrison brought in three of five targets for 40 yards in the Cardinals' 36-30 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
items.s: Harrison was a distant third in receiving yards and tied for the same slotting in targets for the Cardinals on the afternoon. Despite the modest stat line across the board, Harrison's Sunday was certainly an improvement on his Week 2, when he was blanked and saw only one target. While his season-high reception, receiving yardage and target totals offer some solace, they fall short of satisfying frustrated fantasy managers who banked on a comeback campaign from the 2024 first-round pick. Harrison still appears to clearly be behind Michael Wilson and Trey McBride in the Cardinals'…

items.h: Fantasy football: What to do with early-season disappointments like Loveland, Herbert and more
items.s: Matt Bowen discusses players who have struggled early on and offers his level of concern.

items.h: Harrison failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 31-7 loss to the Seahawks.
items.s: Harrison was held without a reception for the second time in three regular-season contests dating back to Week 17 of the 2025 campaign. The wide receiver has now gone four straight regular-season games without recording multiple receptions, and quarterback Jacoby Brissett clearly prefers other options like tight end Trey McBride and fellow wideout Michael Wilson over Harrison again in 2026. It's hard to be confident in the 24-year-old former first-round pick heading into the team's Week 3 matchup with San Francisco.

items.h: Harrison brought in one of three targets for 33 yards in the Cardinals' 26-14 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
items.s: Harrison's one reception was impressive, as he corralled a perfect over-the-shoulder throw from Jacoby Brissett down the left sideline on the Cardinals' second play of the second half to help set up a Chad Ryland field goal. Harrison's low target total was far from ideal, however, as all of Michael Wilson, Kendrick Bourne, Trey McBride and even rookie Jeremiyah Love outpaced him in that regard. Nevertheless, Harrison's upside requires he be kept in fantasy consideration when the Cardinals host the defending champion Seahawks in a Week 2 NFC West clash next Sunday.

items.h: Fantasy Football 'Do Not Draft' list: Giants' young trio among players being overvalued
items.s: The annual hit is back, with players Eric Karabell feels are going earlier than they should in drafts this summer.

items.h: Harrison is listed as a starter on the Cardinals' unofficial depth chart.
items.s: This comes as no surprise considering Harrison's standing as the fourth overall pick in the 2024 Draft and his average of 6.5 targets per game through two seasons in the NFL. However, he has yet to take off, even with QB Jacoby Brissett under center for most of the 2025 campaign, as heel and foot injuries contained him to only three appearances in the final eight contests. Harrison has had a clean bill of health since late July, and with a full training camp working with Brissett and fellow WR Michael Wilson, the trio is set to hit the ground running Week 1 under new coach Mike LaFleur.

items.h: Fantasy football: Answering one key preseason question for 25 NFL teams
items.s: NFL Nation reporters answer the most important fantasy questions, providing insight from training camps.

items.h: Harrison brought in his only target for seven yards and a touchdown and also drew a 20-yard pass interference penalty in the Cardinals' 27-14 preseason win over the Raiders on Thursday.
items.s: The embattled 2024 first-round pick drew the penalty on the Cardinals' third play from scrimmage, and he capped off that opening drive with his seven-yard touchdown grab. Harrison endured an injury-shortened season in 2025 where he suited up for only 12 of 17 regular-season games, but he appears back to full health ahead of what could be a pivotal season for his future with the franchise.

items.h: Harrison (cramps) will practice Tuesday, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Harrison didn't finish practice Sunday due to what coach Mike LaFleur described as cramping. However, the 2024 first-rounder is fine after Monday's day off and will return to the mix Tuesday. As the coming campaign approaches, Harrison will reprise his starting role alongside Michael Wilson. The 23-year-old Harrison is coming off a 2025 regular season in which he caught 41 of 73 passes for 608 yards and four TDs in 12 contests, but if he's able to stay healthy while building a strong rapport with starting QB Jacoby Brissett, his production should take a step forward.

items.h: Harrison (undisclosed) did not finish Arizona's training camp practice on Sunday due to an unknown issue, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
items.s: Harrison reportedly displayed positive chemistry with quarterbacks Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew on Sunday, hauling in a touchdown from the latter during team reps, but the third-year wideout wasn't able to finish the session. It remains to be seen whether Harrison is dealing with an undisclosed injury, or something as minor as conditioning. Arizona will not practice Monday, but Harrison's status will be worth monitoring when the team hosts its first padded session Tuesday.

items.h: Harrison said Tuesday that he is not yet 100 percent recovered from the injuries he dealt with in 2025 but that he doesn't "think it's going to linger into next season, for sure," Josh Weinfuss of ESPN reports.
items.s: Harrison dealt with a number of health issues in 2025, including two heel injuries, a concussion and appendicitis, missing a total of five games spread across the course of the regular season. While the 23-year-old said getting back to full health is "an ongoing process still," he also confirmed that "it's nothing that prevents me from doing anything at the moment" during OTAs. Harrison also stated that health will be his priority this offseason, though a number of other factors will demand his attention as he works to manifest a potential Year 3 leap. In addition to learning a new offense…

items.h: Harrison (foot) participated at Cardinals OTAs this week.
items.s: Harrison sat out Arizona's regular-season finale due to a foot issue that he suffered one week prior, which capped an injury-plagued second pro campaign that contained him to three appearances over the final eight games. Overall, the fourth overall pick in the 2024 Draft followed up a 62-885-8 line on 116 targets in 17 contests as a rookie by hauling in 41 of 73 passes for 608 yards and four TDs in 12 outings last year. With Kyler Murray getting released in March, Harrison will be working with one of the following QBs this fall: Jacoby Brissett (holding out for a reworked contract), newcomer…
